transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-12
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Priya Desai (Redwood AE), Evan Brooks (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Arcadia Head of ML), Diego Ramos (Arcadia CTO), Hannah Lowe (Platform Ops), Raj Patel (Legal)

Summary:
Arcadia is evaluating a 12-month contract extension with a 35% uplift in reserved capacity, plus activation of APAC region (Singapore) for low-latency inference for their diagnostics assistant. Major blockers are procurement timeline, legal language around data residency & KMS custody, and a short technical validation on the Private deployment (VPC + HSM) to prove latency/SLA. Redwood to provide SOW, run a 48-hour private pilot with their KV-cache heavy workload, and provide SOC2 snapshot and KMS integration notes.

Topics discussed:
- Current telemetry and token volumes, sequence lengths for inference
- Dedicated vs Hosted economics and fallback policies
- Private (VPC) onboarding timeline and KMS/HSM options
- APAC region provisioning and expected latency numbers
- Contract language (audit logs, data retention, incident SLA)
- Next steps for procurement and pilot

Action items (captured above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Priya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call. did we get everyone?
[00:06] Maya: yes hi — maya here.
[00:08] Diego: diego on the line.
[00:10] Hannah: hannah, ops.
[00:12] Raj: raj here, legal. short on time but i'll stay for the procurement bits.
[00:16] Priya: awesome. evan, wanna take 1 minute to summarize the pilot ask?
[00:20] Evan: yeah thanks. arcadia asked for a capacity uplift and an APAC node. technical ask is to validate private mode latency at 99th perc under a KV-cache heavy pattern — we suggested a 48-hour run on a dedicated pool with quantized LLM so we can measure p95/p99 and cost delta. also we'll show canary/fallback routing to hosted in case of failover.
[00:41] Diego: two clarifying q's — first, what hardware footprint are you proposing for the dedicated run? second, will model variants be kept consistent with our prod weights? we do retrain frequently.
[00:51] Evan: good call — we can provision a 4x A100-equivalent pool in the private tenant for the run; if you want to mirror production exactly we can deploy the same model artifact URI, otherwise we can use a slightly quantized variant to give a sense of cost/latency tradeoffs. we recommend keeping the model identical for quality checks, run quantized in parallel.
[01:10] Maya: for the diagnostics assistant our seq-lens average 320 tokens, spikes to ~1400 on rare long case notes. how will that affect batching? we've seen other vendors batch aggressively and that increases latency at the tail.
[01:23] Evan: yeah, that's why our runtime does continuous batching with latency SLO controls — you can set a max queue delay so we don't hold requests waiting for a batch. we'll show config samples during the run. another lever is prefix KV caching which should reduce cost for repeated context snippets (e.g., patient meta).
[01:42] Hannah: quick note: our security team is focused on key custody. they'd prefer we hold keys in our HSM but legal said to ask about Redwood KMS options — is that supported in private?
[01:52] Sofia: short answer, yes. private deployments support customer-managed keys via HSM or KMS integrations; during onboarding we can wire up your HSM through our onprem connector or use your cloud KMS with a customer-managed envelope. we'll include a KMS runbook.
[02:06] Raj: on contract front, we need explicit language about data residency for APAC; Arcadia needs to ensure PHI stays within SG region and that audit logs are retained 7 years. also need incident notification windows and SLA credits clearly stated.
[02:19] Priya: noted — our standard addendum for data residency covers region pinning + audit log retention; i'll slot the 7-year retention as an explicit ask and send a redline. on SLAs we can propose 99.5 uptime for Dedicated with credits on breach; frank to engineering will confirm p99 latency targets.
[02:36] Diego: another procurement question — what about burst capacity? if we commit to reserved capacity can we still burst to hosted in a controlled way?
[02:45] Evan: yes, we support burst to hosted with routing policies — you can set cost thresholds and region preferences. fallback maintains model-compatible variants so output quality should be similar; there is a small delta if the hosted model is quantized differently but we can tie the policy to prefer compatibility.
[02:59] Maya: do we have benchmark numbers for Singapore region when using APAC nodes? our users are mostly in SEA and Australia.
[03:06] Evan: preliminary numbers: p95 ~ 60–80ms for standard gen on APAC nodes for short seqs, p99 ~ 150–220ms depending on model size and KV cache hits. for your seq-lens average the p99 will be higher — we'll run the real test to give you exact figures.
[03:24] Hannah: operationally, how long to provision a private cluster in SG once we sign? we have a tight runway — would like minimal lead time.
[03:32] Sofia: typical provisioning is 7–14 business days for VPC peering, capacity allocation, and KMS wiring; if we pre-approve infra we can accelerate to 3–5 days but that depends on your cloud account setup.
[03:44] Raj: any compliance docs we can get ahead of time? SOC2, ISO, penetration test reports, third party audit?
[03:50] Priya: yes i'll attach the security pack (SOC2 report, ISO summary, pen-test redacted report) to the SOW. we can also provide our SOC2 snapshot and auditor contact under an NDA.
[03:59] Diego: cost math — tends to be the sticking point. can you illustrate delta between hosted token cost vs dedicated reserved + burst?
[04:07] Priya: absolutely — i'll include a tiered pricing sheet that shows nominal per-token hosted rates, reserved monthly capacity pricing, and a blended cost for 35% uplift with 10% burst usage. we'll model with your current token counts. please share the last 30 days of telemetry after the call so i can plug numbers in.
[04:23] Maya: i'll export usage — one note, we have a lot of embedding calls for triage; those are CPU-heavy not GPU. are there separate billing buckets?
[04:31] Priya: yes embeddings are billed differently; we'll segregate embedding unit pricing and show expected monthly spend in the SOW.
[04:38] Diego: can we get a small A/B test to validate quality between quantized and full-fp model? some of our clinicians noticed hallucinations with quantized variants elsewhere.
[04:48] Evan: we'll run parallel A/B during the 48h test: identical prompts across both variants, diff flags; we'll produce delta metrics (ROUGE-ish proxies, clinician sampling notes) and raw generated outputs.
[04:59] Hannah: during the pilot, what telemetry will Redwood surface? we need token-level cost, per-route latency, and error traces.
[05:07] Evan: Redwood Console gives per-route cost/latency, token breakdown, trace IDs, and a raw events stream. we'll provide access to an ephemeral dashboard for the pilot.
[05:15] Raj: need to clarify data deletion policy post-pilot — do logs persist by default?
[05:20] Sofia: retention defaults to 90 days, but for pilot we can set shorter retention or provide an export and then purge. we'll confirm the purge procedure in the runbook.
[05:30] Priya: okay let's talk timeline. arcadia — your desired decision window?
[05:34] Maya: ideally sign by end of month — but procurement needs solid numbers and legal needs the redline. so realistically 3 weeks.
[05:40] Raj: yes three weeks sounds right. we might ask for a 2-week extension if internal signatories are slow.
[05:45] Priya: understood. we'll aim to get SOW and pricing by monday 2025-03-16 and start the pilot after SOW acceptance — pilot target start 2025-03-18 assuming infra approvals.
[05:55] Diego: who will own the pilot on redwood side?
[05:58] Priya: evan will run the pilot, sofia will run onboarding and CSM tasks, and i will handle contract and pricing.
[06:05] Evan: quick technical note — for KV cache heavy patterns we recommend enabling prefix caching and a small warmup run for cache population; that often cuts token costs 20–30% for recurrent patient metadata.
[06:18] Maya: good to know. please include a cache-warmup script we can run during the pilot.
[06:23] Evan: will do.
[06:25] [08:15] Diego: slight crosstalk, sorry. switching to legal detail — are you amenable to a data processing addendum (DPA) that specifies sub-processors and cross-border transfer mechanisms?
[08:28] Priya: yes we have a standard DPA; for APAC we'll include Singapore region sub-processor list and SCCs where applicable.
[08:36] Raj: and for incident response: we need a 4-hour initial notification SLA and full incident report within 72 hours.
[08:44] Sofia: we can accommodate a 4-hour initial notification for P1 incidents; full write-ups are typically 72 hours, might be extended depending on forensic needs.
[08:53] Maya: moving back to ops — for blue/green rollouts in production, what's your rollback time if a model regression is detected?
[08:59] Evan: we have canary deployments with automatic rollback on quality regression tied to eval sets; typical rollback is under 10 minutes to redirect traffic, 30–45 minutes to fully revert state if warm caches need rebuild. we'll demo the rollout flow in a follow-up tech session.
[09:19] Diego: do you support staged rollouts by customer segment? we have internal vs clinician flows and want staged exposure.
[09:26] Evan: yes route-level routing and per-token quotas let you slice exposure; canary to 5% then 25% then full.
[09:33] Hannah: about AWS peering — we need a hardened peering config and egress rules to lock down logs; can your VPC peering accommodate restricted subnets?
[09:42] Sofia: yes we support restricted subnets and can provide Terraform templates for the peering and security groups.
[09:49] Priya: i'm seeing one question in chat — will enabling HSM increase RTO for key rotation?
[09:56] Evan: HSMs add a slight latency on crypto ops but shouldn't materially affect inference latency; key rotation is a background operation and doesn't block in-flight inference. we'll document rotation steps.
[10:06] Maya: any concerns about vendor lock-in if we go private? we don't want a heavy lift to move later.
[10:13] Priya: our private offering aims to keep artifacts portable — model artifacts are stored as URIs and we provide export tooling for KV caches and prompt templates. moving workloads will still need provisioning elsewhere but we try to minimize lock-in.
[10:24] Diego: can you share a migration checklist?
[10:26] Priya: yes will include a migration playbook in the SOW.
[10:29] [20:40] Evan: i'm going to call out a couple of risks from engineering: cold-start p99 during massive bursts, and cache edge-cases if your prompts include large attachments. we'll instrument and monitor those during the pilot.
[20:52] Maya: attachments are rare but sometimes we include base64 PDF snippets; does KV store support that size?
[20:58] Evan: we handle reference pointers to object storage rather than storing blobs in KV; better to pass references. we'll recommend patterns.
[21:10] Raj: back to contract: we might want a clause for model output auditability for regulatory purposes — are you able to log model inputs/outputs in an immutable audit trail?
[21:20] Sofia: yes we capture request/response audit logs with trace IDs; for regulatory we can support an append-only log export and time-stamped snapshots. export process will be part of onboarding.
[21:31] Priya: wrap-up, folks — double-check next steps: i'll send SOW + security pack by 2025-03-16; evan will schedule and run the 48-hour private pilot starting ~2025-03-18 pending infra; hannah to confirm KMS preference; raj to send legal must-haves; maya/diego to share last 30-day telemetry.
[21:54] Maya: confirmed. we'll get telemetry and the embedding usage broken out.
[22:00] Diego: also we'll identify one clinician for quality spot-checking during the A/B.
[22:05] Hannah: i'll align infra team and provide AWS account contacts tomorrow.
[22:10] Raj: i'll try to get procurement slot for 3/24; if not, 3/31.
[22:15] Priya: great — thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot kickoff and a legal touchpoint.

End: 16:52 UTC
